questions.question: Why does React Testing Library encourage querying by text/label/role instead of class names?
options: Querying the way a user would interacts with the DOM keeps tests valid even after restyling the component
Class names are not supported in JSX
questions.explanation: Testing Library's philosophy is to test what the user sees/does, so tests don't break from unrelated implementation changes like renamed CSS classes.

questions.question: What kind of bug is Playwright end-to-end testing best suited to catch that a unit test typically can't?
options: A typo in a single component's prop type
An integration failure across a real user flow, like routing + a Server Action + the database together
questions.explanation: E2E tests drive a real browser against a running app, exercising full flows (e.g. login navigating to a protected dashboard) that unit tests, which isolate one component, don't cover.

questions.question: What determines whether an environment variable is exposed to client-side JavaScript in Next.js?
options: Whether its name is prefixed with NEXT_PUBLIC_
Whether it's used inside a Server Component
All environment variables are exposed to the client by default
questions.explanation: Only NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed variables get inlined into the browser bundle; anything else stays server-only, which is why secrets must never carry that prefix.

questions.question: What does Vercel typically create for every pull request on a connected repository?
options: Nothing, until it's merged to production
A unique preview deployment for reviewing that PR's changes before merging
A rollback of the previous deployment
questions.explanation: Preview deployments give every PR its own working environment with a unique URL, separate from the production deployment.
